title: Predictive Coalescer: workload-centric batching policy generator and safe rollout
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a Predictive Coalescer: a policy generator that produces workload-specific batching and KV-cache policies using continuous profiling and lightweight heuristics, with a robust safe-apply and automatic rollback pipeline. This ticket covers the end-to-end engine: data collection, feature extraction, heuristic policy synthesis, the continuous annealer that tunes parameters, and a controller to shadow-apply / canary / rollback policies with SLO gates.
background_and_problem_statement: Current recommended batching profiles are static and applied manually; customers and Dedicated clusters see suboptimal unit cost or manual misconfigurations causing either inflated latency or wasted GPU cycles. We need an automated generator which understands workload temporal patterns, coalesces small requests safely, and continuously adapts parameters while guaranteeing SLOs and clear rollback semantics.
goals: Automate per-tenant/per-route batching and KV-cache suggestions from live telemetry
Achieve >=5% cost-per-token improvement on targeted mixed workloads without >5% p95 latency regression
Provide shadow-apply and canary rollout with automated rollback based on SLO gates
Expose explainability signals for each generated policy (why this profile was chosen)
out_of_scope: Model-level quantization recommendations (handled by Optimize team)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline implements telemetry collection for batch-size, queue-time, token-cost, and per-request latency
Policy generator produces human-readable policy artifacts (batch_size_bounds, max_delay_ms, kv_cache_prefetch) and a confidence score
Shadow-apply runs for 48h without affecting live traffic; metrics collected and compared
Canary rollout can be configured to N% traffic and will auto-rollback if p95 latency increases >2% or error rate increases >0.5ppt
Integration tests cover corner cases: ultra-low-latency routes, bursty request patterns, and KV-cache invalidation windows
Dashboard widgets show historical policy decisions and rollout status
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Data & Spike (2w): wire telemetry, build feature extractor, run offline profiling on 10 representative workloads
Phase 2 - Heuristic Synthesizer (2w): implement rule-based policy generator using workload percentiles and cost-latency tradeoffs
Phase 3 - Continuous Annealer (3w): light-weight feedback loop that nudges parameters based on observed deltas (cost, latency), with safety bounds
Phase 4 - Safe Apply Controller (2w): shadow-apply, canary controller, SLO gating, and automatic rollback logic integrated with Console
Phase 5 - Hardening & Rollout (2w): integration tests, runbook, rollout docs, and internal beta with 3 customers
telemetry_and_metrics: p50/p95 latency when coalesced vs baseline
rollout_strategy: Start with shadow-apply for 48 hours with synthetic traffic and measure divergence
Canary apply to 5% of traffic for 24 hours with active SLO gates
If canary passes, ramp to 25% for 48h, then 100% with staged ramp-up over 3 days
Immediate automated rollback on SLO breach + manual alert to oncall
Post-rollout review and store accepted policy as baseline for next annealing cycle
safety_and_guardrails: Per-route upper bounds for max_delay_ms to limit added latency
Minimum reserved batch trigger to avoid starving low-volume, latency-sensitive routes
SLO gating thresholds defined per-customer and per-tier (hosted vs dedicated)
Shadow mode must not alter live request path or KV invalidation windows
Audit log entries for every policy change linked to rollout id and author
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Coalescing increases tail latency for a subset of routes -> Mitigation: conservative initial max_delay_ms and canary gating
Risk: KV prefetch may increase memory pressure -> Mitigation: cap prefetch window and measure hit-rate before enabling widely
Risk: Incorrect telemetry skewing policies -> Mitigation: bootstrap with conservative heuristics and ensemble of short-term and long-term stats
Risk: Automated rollback flapping -> Mitigation: implement cooldown and require two consecutive SLO breaches before hard rollback
open_questions: How to parameterize policies for multi-model pipelines (router->adapter->model)?
Should confidence scores be exposed to customers or only surfaced to operator consoles?
What is the right cadence for annealing (real-time vs hourly vs daily) given telemetry noise?

2026-03-02 Design review with runtime & console teams. Agreed to expose policy diffs in Console and to keep shadow mode strictly passive.

2026-03-05 Spike results: prototype reduced avg token cost by ~12% on p3-mix workload but increased p95 by 3.7% on one low-latency route; we added an early-exit threshold to avoid applying to routes with p95 < 15ms.
2026-03-07 Architecture note: heuristics synthesizer will emit a confidence score and rationale (percentiles used). Runtime will reject policies with confidence < 0.2 by default.
2026-03-09 PR opened with initial synthesizer and feature extractor (github.com/.../pull/42). Requesting review from @runtime-oncall and @console-eng.
2026-03-11 QA: Integration tests added; discovered KV prefetch spike on heavy-mesh test — mitigation implemented by capping simultaneous prefetches per-GPU.
2026-03-12 PM review by Jordan Lee: Approved for canary scheduling. Canaries targeted to non-critical routes and 3 pilot customers. Added to Cycle 2026-W10.
